events.title: Neolithic Settlement
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human activity in the UAE region during the Neolithic period. Early settlements were found along the coast, with inhabitants engaged in fishing and simple agriculture. These early residents made pottery and stone tools.

events.title: Umm al-Nar Civilization
events.description: The UAE region was inhabited during the Bronze Age, with the Umm al-Nar culture flourishing. Archaeological discoveries show trade links with Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley. The region's copper mines and pearls were important trade commodities.

events.title: Umm al-Nar Tombs
events.description: Numerous Umm al-Nar period collective tombs discovered in Abu Dhabi reveal complex social structures and trade networks. Tombs contained goods from Mesopotamia, India and Central Asia, proving the region's importance in ancient trade.

events.title: Iron Age
events.description: The UAE entered the Iron Age, with agricultural and irrigation technology developing. The Falaj irrigation system began to be used, an underground water channel system still in use in Oman and parts of the UAE today.

events.title: Persian Sassanid Influence
events.description: The UAE region was influenced by the Persian Sassanid Empire, becoming part of the Persian Gulf trade network. Christianity was introduced during this period, with archaeological sites showing monasteries and churches.

events.title: Nestorian Christianity
events.description: Nestorian Christianity established churches and monasteries in the UAE region. Important Christian sites discovered on Sir Bani Yas Island, including church and monastery ruins, prove the region was a center of Christian activity.

events.title: Islamization
events.description: The UAE region converted to Islam during Prophet Muhammad's time. The Battle of Dibba (632 CE) was an important early Islamic battle in the region. The UAE became part of the Islamic Caliphate, gradually Arabizing.

events.title: Arab Caliphate Era
events.description: The UAE region prospered under Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates. Pearl diving industry developed, coastal towns like Julfar (now Ras Al Khaimah) became important trading ports. The region had active trade with India, China and East Africa.

events.title: Hormuz Kingdom Influence
events.description: The Persian Hormuz Kingdom controlled Persian Gulf trade, significantly influencing UAE coastal areas. Regional ports became important nodes connecting East-West trade. Pearl and spice trade flourished.

events.title: Portuguese Arrival
events.description: After Vasco da Gama rounded the Cape of Good Hope, Portugal began expanding in the Persian Gulf. In 1515, Portugal occupied Hormuz, controlling the Persian Gulf entrance. Portugal attempted to monopolize spice trade, conflicting with local tribes.

events.title: European Colonial Competition
events.description: Portugal, Netherlands and Britain competed for control of the Persian Gulf. Portugal briefly controlled parts of the coast, but local tribes resisted. The region's strategic location made it a focus of European powers.

events.title: Omani Expansion
events.description: After expelling the Portuguese, the Omani Yaruba dynasty expanded its influence to UAE coastal areas. Oman controlled many ports and forts, but inland desert areas remained under Bedouin tribal control.

events.title: Bani Yas Establish Abu Dhabi
events.description: A branch of the Bani Yas tribe, the Nahyan family, settled on Abu Dhabi island after discovering fresh water. Abu Dhabi gradually developed into an important pearl diving and trading center.

events.title: Maktoum Family Establish Dubai
events.description: The Maktoum family migrated from Abu Dhabi to the Dubai Creek, establishing Dubai emirate. Dubai developed as an important trading port due to its excellent harbor, attracting merchants from India, Persia and the Arabian Peninsula.

events.title: Qawasim Tribal Federation
events.description: The Qawasim tribe established a strong maritime power in Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, controlling lower Persian Gulf shipping. They challenged British and Omani maritime hegemony. Britain called them 'pirates,' but Qawasim considered themselves legitimate maritime power.

events.title: First British Military Expedition
events.description: The British East India Company sent a fleet to attack Ras Al Khaimah, destroying Qawasim fleet and fortifications. But Qawasim quickly rebuilt, continuing to challenge British control in the Persian Gulf.

events.title: Decisive British Expedition
events.description: Britain launched a larger military operation, decisively defeating Qawasim naval power. Multiple coastal fortifications were destroyed, fleets burned. This expedition forced Qawasim and other sheikhs to negotiate with Britain.

events.title: General Maritime Treaty
events.description: After multiple British naval expeditions against 'pirates,' coastal sheikhs signed treaty with Britain ending maritime raids. The region was called the 'Trucial Coast.' Britain protected emirates from external threats in exchange for control of foreign affairs and defense.

events.title: Perpetual Maritime Truce
events.description: Sheikhs signed more comprehensive treaty with Britain, establishing permanent peace and recognizing Britain as protector. Trucial Coast emirates became British protectorate, relationship lasting until 1971.

events.title: Exclusive Agreements
events.description: Sheikhs agreed not to enter agreements with any country except Britain, giving Britain complete control of foreign affairs. This consolidated British dominance in the region, excluding Ottoman, Persian and other powers.

events.title: Golden Age of Pearl Industry
events.description: Early 20th century was golden age of Persian Gulf pearl industry. Thousands of pearling boats and tens of thousands of divers participated in pearl harvesting. Dubai and Abu Dhabi exported pearls to Europe, India and Far East, bringing wealth to emirates.

events.title: Pearl Industry Collapse
events.description: Japanese cultured pearls and Great Depression caused collapse of Persian Gulf pearl industry. Pearls were the region's main economic pillar, collapse causing severe economic hardship. Many residents fell into poverty, population decreased.

events.title: World War II Impact
events.description: During WWII, Trucial Coast was relatively quiet, but Britain strengthened military presence to protect Persian Gulf oil supply routes. The region became rear base for British Middle East Command. Post-war British influence began to wane.

events.title: Trucial States Council Established
events.description: Britain helped establish Trucial States Council, providing consultation platform for seven emirates. This was first institutionalized cooperation among emirates, laying foundation for later federation.

events.title: Oil Discovery in Abu Dhabi
events.description: Umm Shaif oil field discovered offshore Abu Dhabi, marking turning point in region's destiny. Oil exports began in 1962. Oil revenues completely transformed Abu Dhabi and later UAE, from impoverished desert to one of world's wealthiest regions.

events.title: Abu Dhabi Oil Exports Begin
events.description: Abu Dhabi's first oil exports marked beginning of economic transformation. Oil revenues grew rapidly, but early development was slow under conservative management of ruler Sheikh Shakhbut.

events.title: Dubai Oil Discovery
events.description: Oil discovered in Dubai's Fateh field, though reserves far less than Abu Dhabi, provided Dubai with development funds. Dubai ruler Rashid wisely invested oil revenues in infrastructure and trade facilities.

events.title: Sheikh Zayed Becomes Ruler of Abu Dhabi
events.description: Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan overthrew his brother, becoming ruler of Abu Dhabi. Zayed began large-scale modernization with oil revenues, building schools, hospitals, roads and housing. He later became UAE's founding father.

events.title: Britain Announces Withdrawal
events.description: Britain announced withdrawal from east of Suez by 1971, including Persian Gulf. This forced Trucial Coast emirates to consider their future. Initially planned nine-state federation with Bahrain and Qatar, but ultimately failed.

events.title: Formation of UAE
events.description: Six emirates (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm al-Quwain, Fujairah) formed the United Arab Emirates, with Zayed elected first president. Ras al-Khaimah joined in 1972, forming seven emirates. UAE adopted federal system, each emirate retaining considerable autonomy.

events.title: Joining UN and Arab League
events.description: After independence, UAE quickly gained international recognition, joining United Nations and Arab League. UAE began actively participating in international affairs, particularly in Arab and Islamic world matters.

events.title: Ras Al Khaimah Joins Federation
events.description: After two months of observation, Ras Al Khaimah finally decided to join UAE, becoming the seventh emirate. This completed the unification of Trucial States, forming today's UAE.

events.title: Oil Boom
events.description: 1973 oil crisis caused oil prices to soar, UAE gained huge revenues. Zayed invested in massive infrastructure: roads, ports, airports, schools, hospitals. Abu Dhabi and Dubai rapidly transformed from desert towns to modern cities.

events.title: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company
events.description: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) was established, integrating Abu Dhabi's oil assets. ADNOC gradually became one of world's largest oil companies, controlling most of UAE's oil production.

events.title: Dubai World Trade Centre
events.description: Dubai World Trade Centre completed at 149 meters, tallest building in Middle East at the time. This landmark building symbolized Dubai's modernization ambitions, becoming catalyst for Dubai's commercial development.

events.title: Joining Gulf Cooperation Council
events.description: UAE, with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and Oman, co-founded Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to promote economic and security cooperation. GCC became important platform for Gulf states to coordinate policies.

events.title: Emirates Airline Founded
events.description: Dubai established Emirates airline, initially with only two leased aircraft. With government support and market-oriented operations, Emirates rapidly grew into one of world's largest international airlines, making Dubai a global aviation hub.

events.title: Gulf War Participation
events.description: After Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, UAE joined US-led coalition. UAE provided military bases, funding and troops. This consolidated UAE's strategic alliance with the West, especially the United States.

events.title: BCCI Banking Scandal
events.description: Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), headquartered in Abu Dhabi, collapsed due to money laundering and fraud scandals. This event prompted UAE to strengthen financial regulation and improve financial system transparency.

events.title: Dubai Economic Diversification
events.description: Dubai ruler Mohammed bin Rashid promoted economic diversification, developing trade, tourism, aviation and finance. Dubai built world-class infrastructure: Jebel Ali Port, Emirates Airlines, Dubai World Trade Centre. Dubai became Middle East business hub.

events.title: Sheikh Mohammed Becomes Crown Prince of Dubai
events.description: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum was appointed Crown Prince of Dubai and UAE Defense Minister. He began leading Dubai's development strategy, promoting economic diversification and modernization.

events.title: Dubai Internet City and Media City
events.description: Dubai established free zones like Dubai Internet City and Media City, attracting international companies like Microsoft, IBM and CNN. These free zones offered 100% foreign ownership, tax exemption and modern regulation, becoming key to Dubai's economic diversification.

events.title: Jebel Ali Free Zone Expansion
events.description: Jebel Ali Free Zone underwent massive expansion, becoming Middle East's largest free zone. Over 5,000 companies established operations, covering manufacturing, logistics and services. Jebel Ali Port became one of world's busiest container ports.

events.title: Dubai International Financial Centre
events.description: Dubai established Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), adopting English common law system to attract international financial institutions. DIFC became Middle East's main financial center, competing with London and New York.

events.title: Death of Sheikh Zayed
events.description: UAE founding father Sheikh Zayed died aged 86. He transformed UAE from poor tribal confederation to modern prosperous nation. His eldest son Khalifa bin Zayed succeeded as UAE president and Abu Dhabi ruler.

events.title: First National Elections
events.description: UAE held its first limited elections to select some Federal National Council members. Though voting rights were restricted (only about 6,700 could vote), this was a small step in UAE's political reform.

events.title: Mohammed Becomes Dubai Ruler
events.description: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum became Dubai ruler and UAE Vice President and Prime Minister. He continued Dubai's ambitious development, promoting mega projects like Palm Islands, Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall.

events.title: Financial Crisis Impact
events.description: Global financial crisis hit Dubai hard, real estate bubble burst, debt crisis threatened companies like Dubai World. Abu Dhabi provided tens of billions in assistance, helping Dubai weather crisis. Crisis forced Dubai to plan development more carefully.

events.title: Burj Khalifa Completion
events.description: Dubai completed world's tallest building Burj Khalifa (originally Dubai Tower), 828 meters high. This iconic building symbolizes UAE's ambition and modernization. Despite financial crisis, project completed, demonstrating UAE resilience.

events.title: Dubai Metro Opens
events.description: Dubai Metro Red Line opened, Middle East's first fully automated metro system. Metro system eases traffic congestion, supporting Dubai's urban development. Green Line opened in 2011.

events.title: Khalifa Port Construction Begins
events.description: Abu Dhabi began constructing Khalifa Port, Middle East's first semi-automated container terminal. Port began operations in 2012, enhancing Abu Dhabi's logistics and trade capabilities.

events.title: Arab Spring and Stability
events.description: Although Arab Spring swept Middle East, UAE remained stable. Government arrested political activists and Muslim Brotherhood members, preventing dissent. UAE's wealth, welfare and authoritarian control kept it immune from turmoil.

events.title: Dubai Mall Expansion
events.description: Dubai Mall completed expansion, becoming one of world's largest malls with over 80 million annual visitors. Mall features aquarium, ice rink and hundreds of shops, becoming global tourist destination.

events.title: Dubai Wins Expo 2020 Bid
events.description: Dubai defeated Brazil, Russia and Turkey to win 2020 World Expo hosting rights. First Expo in Middle East, themed 'Connecting Minds, Creating the Future.' Expo postponed to 2021 due to pandemic.

events.title: Yemen War Intervention
events.description: UAE joined Saudi-led coalition intervening in Yemen against Houthi forces. UAE deployed ground troops, playing key role in southern Yemen. But war costly and inconclusive, UAE began withdrawal in 2019.

events.title: Louvre Abu Dhabi
events.description: Louvre Abu Dhabi Museum began construction, France's Louvre's first overseas branch. Museum opened in 2017, displaying artworks from around the world, symbolizing UAE's cultural ambitions.

events.title: Qatar Diplomatic Crisis
events.description: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Egypt severed ties with Qatar, accusing it of supporting terrorism and close Iran ties. Blockade lasted until 2021, UAE played hardline role in pushing blockade. Crisis exposed Gulf states divisions.

events.title: Long-term Visa Program
events.description: UAE launched long-term visa program, offering 5-10 year visas for investors, entrepreneurs, scientists and outstanding students. Program aims to attract and retain talent, supporting economic diversification.

events.title: Year of Tolerance
events.description: UAE declared 2019 'Year of Tolerance,' emphasizing coexistence among different cultures and religions. Abu Dhabi built Abrahamic Family House, housing mosque, church and synagogue.

events.title: Abraham Accords
events.description: UAE became third Arab country to normalize relations with Israel (after Egypt, Jordan). Agreement signed at White House, Trump brokered. Normalization includes diplomacy, trade, tourism and security cooperation. UAE said move prevents Israeli West Bank annexation, but Palestinians condemned as betrayal.

events.title: Mars Mission
events.description: UAE's Hope Probe successfully entered Mars orbit, making UAE fifth nation to reach Mars. This demonstrated UAE's ambition in technology and space, celebrating UAE's 50th anniversary.

events.title: Barakah Nuclear Power Plant Starts
events.description: Arab world's first nuclear power plant, Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, began operations in Abu Dhabi. Plant consists of four reactors, will provide 25% of UAE's electricity needs, supporting energy diversification.

events.title: Rise of Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohammed
events.description: Mohammed bin Zayed (MBZ) became UAE's de facto ruler as President Khalifa's health declined. MBZ pursued decisive foreign policy, playing major regional role, supporting anti-Islamist forces. He's considered one of Gulf's most powerful leaders.

events.title: Gulf Reconciliation
events.description: UAE reconciled with Qatar under Saudi leadership, ending four-year diplomatic crisis. Borders reopened, relations normalized. This showed Gulf states seeking unity when facing common challenges.

events.title: Expo 2020 Dubai Opens
events.description: After one-year pandemic delay, Expo 2020 Dubai opened, lasting six months. 192 countries participated, attracting over 24 million visitors. Expo showcased Dubai and UAE's organizational capacity and international standing.

events.title: Mohamed Becomes President
events.description: After President Khalifa's death, Mohamed bin Zayed was elected UAE's third president. Transition smooth, continuing Zayed family leadership of UAE. MBZ continues advancing UAE's economic diversification and regional influence.

events.title: COP28 Climate Summit
events.description: UAE hosted UN COP28 climate conference, controversial as UAE is major oil producer. But summit reached historic agreement calling for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels.' UAE simultaneously invests in renewable energy, building world's largest solar power plants.

events.title: Economic Diversification and Future Vision
events.description: UAE continues economic diversification, reducing oil dependence (oil only 30% of GDP). Dubai is global hub for trade, tourism, aviation and finance. Abu Dhabi invests in renewable energy, technology and culture (Louvre Abu Dhabi). UAE attracts millions of expatriates, population 90% foreign. UAE faces challenges: human rights issues, labor rights, climate change and regional tensions. But UAE remains one of Middle East's most stable and prosperous nations, leveraging strategic location, wealth and visionary leadership.
